recognize_zh: 這顆淋巴球細胞質較豐富、淡藍，箭頭處細胞質內有一根細長透明、不著色的針狀結構，靠近核緣；這種負像棒狀物是惡性淋巴球內的結晶包涵體。
features: Medium-to-large lymphoid cell with moderate N:C ratio
Oval nucleus with moderately coarse, clumped chromatin; no distinct nucleolus
Moderate amount of pale blue cytoplasm
Slender, colorless needle-like crystal in the cytoplasm near the nuclear border (arrow)
No cytoplasmic granules or vacuoles; digitally enlarged image
describe_en: High-power, digitally enlarged view of a peripheral blood smear shows a lymphoid cell with an oval nucleus, moderately clumped chromatin and a moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm. A thin, unstained, needle-shaped crystalline inclusion is present within the cytoplasm alongside the nucleus (arrow). There are no azurophilic granules, vacuoles or Auer rods. Findings are consistent with a crystalline inclusion in a malignant lymphocyte, a feature of low-grade B-cell lymphoproliferative disorders with abnormal immunoglobulin accumulation; confirmation relies on flow cytometry and, if needed, electron microscopy.

ddx.vs: Auer rods stain pink-red to purple and occur in myeloblasts or promyelocytes with fine chromatin, not as colorless clefts in mature lymphoid cells.
Reactive lymphocytes may have similar cytoplasm but lack crystalline inclusions.
Crystal-storing histiocytes are much larger tissue cells with abundant cytoplasm packed with crystals, not a circulating lymphocyte with a single rod.
